Maintenance Report — MNT-0014-004

Asset: WELL-0014 (SW-23 Well 014, T350, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: separator Work started: 09 Nov 2024 08:00 · Finished: 20 Nov 2024 07:00 · Well stopped for this job: 263 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Kevin Price Triggered by: inspection INS-0014-0019 on 2024-11-07 Report written: 21 Nov 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the separator was overfilling and the dump valve was not opening. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0014-0019 showed the wellhead at 25.4 °C with the air at 19.7 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The level controller had failed. The well stayed shut in for about 9 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

Paraffin build-up stopped the float from moving.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Isolated and depressurised the separator.
  2. Replaced the level controller.
  3. Calibrated the controller and tested the dump valve.

Summary of the fix: replaced level controller.

Testing and return to service

Cycled the separator three times; level control worked correctly. The well was returned to production.

maintenance.action: Replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil
maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0014-009

Asset: WELL-0014 (SW-23 Well 014, T350, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: flowline Work started: 16 May 2025 08:00 · Finished: 16 May 2025 18:00 · Well stopped for this job: 10 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Brian Coleman Triggered by: inspection INS-0014-0044 on 2025-05-15 Report written: 16 May 2025

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0014-0044 at 10:30 on 2025-05-15 found crude oil on the pad: about 5.0% of the pad area, estimated 2.0 bbl. The inspector noted: "Pooled fluid near flowline." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 7.2 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Corrosion under a failed protective wrap on the coupling.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 1 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 2% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 340 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 272 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 1.8 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0014-009 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.64% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

maintenance.action: Replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit
maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0014-015

Asset: WELL-0014 (SW-23 Well 014, T350, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 26 Jul 2026 08:00 · Finished: 29 Jul 2026 15:00 · Well stopped for this job: 79 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Daniel Foster Triggered by: inspection INS-0014-0106 on 2026-07-23 Report written: 31 Jul 2026

What happened

Field staff reported that the motor breaker kept tripping and the pump jack would not run. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0014-0106 showed the wellhead at 48.7 °C with the air at 38.3 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit. The well stayed shut in for about 1 day longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

Root cause

Moisture got into the motor terminal box and damaged the windings.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 1 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
  2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
  3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
  4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours; motor current within the nameplate rating and stroke rate normal. The well was returned to production.
